title: What would be the most impressive game AI could create today?
author: sharkymcstevenson2
selftext:
I'm looking for inspiration for my next game build and want input from you guys, 

What would be the most impressive example of an AI-made game that you could think of?

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: I have a project I'm working on that I plan to share soon that I think looks impressive but if I had to answer the question, I'm not really sure what game you couldn't make. The most impressive game would be the one you want to make. You won't get very far trying to just make someone else's game

replies.author: pennystudio
replies.body: I agree, it's not bottlenecked by AI. It's bottlenecked by your imagination, the hours you are willing to put in, and execution.

comments.author: No-Marionberry-772
comments.body:
narrative driven action adventure that is actually compelling with engaging movement and combat mechanics.


Think the Original God of War, or Darksiders 1.


Getting purpose specific items that drive gameplay and are provided as story elements that bridge the gameplay and the narrative.


This requires sooo many things to be done right, but when done right is peak gaming.


If that can be built, be compelling and engaging for both story and gameplay, its the signal that AI has truly arived, for game dev atleast.

comments.author: Critical_Hunter_6924
comments.body: anything? wtf are you asking lol

comments.author: miomao10
comments.body:
Tbh it can do anything in any genre. All it takes is your constraints and ideas.  
I plan to launch games in every genre

comments.author: Individual_Review771
comments.body: i would say on the level of gta 3 if you know how to use a game engine and don't just straight up send ai your entire game file to prompt. If you learn to send segments or seperate files then you can make a game with 10s of thousands of lines of code

comments.author: siendo64
comments.body: All depends how much work you’re going to put into it yourself and how you plan to leverage AI to create it. Tell us more about what kind of workflow you want to use

comments.author: ProfessorChalupa
comments.body: I would be more impressed by a step-by-step guide using innovative/novel orchestration and workflows with minimal to no manual work needed to build some of the games mentioned here.  The architecture side of things.  At least that’s what I’m inspired to do  seeing all the cool shit being built here.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: I know this sounds crazy but once you have Claude code setup, it's literally like just talking to a game designer. I describe the system I want to implement, I describe the overall design of the game, I talk it through bugging fixes and UI design, I show it pictures of concepts or issues. It's like working with someone who understands what you're conveying. You don't need secret sentence structure or incredible vernacular to get the AI to do what. It's much smarter than it used to be. Maybe I can include something like this though when I show the game I'm working on

replies.author: ProfessorChalupa
replies.body: Cool, yea I get that, but I mean fine-tuning skills, subagents, hooks and the like and also workflows with code repos, security checking, testing, MCP server use - I’ve tried Unity + Blender + Gimp for a concept 80’s metal 3D third-person game and it turned out to be more like 1989’s MadMaze hosted on Prodigy than anything modern.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: Well yeah but you can just ask Claude. That's how I set up my MCPs but I'll be honest Claude was not very successful in blender but I found Claude to be quite good at making mock meshes in unity. It's definitely not at a point where you can leave the entire game design to AI though. But as for fine tuning skills and sub agents and hooks I'm not sure what those are needed for, do you have a better description?

comments.author: KidLink4
comments.body:
I think there's a weird misconception that everyone doing ai dev is just one shotting. That's absolutely not the case in most scenarios. In a correct setup, even the phrasing of the question is wrong - AI isn't the creator, it's the keyboard. 

The answer to your question though, is that the sky is the limit - that and your patience

comments.body:
A framework for converting open source map data into game world. Basically I want ms flight sim but for driving cars/motorcycles. 

I kinda got it working with AI.

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: Something like Skyrim but roguelike type, like every time you play you get a different main story, the npcs can talk and think in the context of that story and missions, characters and the environment change according to your decisions.

replies.author: sharkymcstevenson2
replies.body: Yeah agree, a fully fleshed out Skyrim would be a pretty big holy \*\*\*\* moment

comments.author: ProfessorChalupa
comments.body:
Noted on the meshes tip. I’ll give that a shot.

Game development has a bunch of roles - there’s a designer, in-game “AI” programmer, game developer, level engineer, gameplay mechanics engineer.  The skills break down exactly what each role would manage, so then you don’t have to re-explain the concepts every time — it know that for this particular game, here are the parameters and guardrails to follow.  Hooks are safeguards to run functional tests, security checks (although, Opus 4.7 sorta has this built in now since no one does it), line length limits per file, etc.  Subagents are the ones that act as the personas/roles, read the skill and execute accordingly from your prompt and the skill reference

comments.author: SaltAfternoon9986
comments.body:
Something like borderlands or Skyrim, with huge cohesive worlds, npcs, storylines and quality combat probably

  
that or WoW lol

comments.author: MakeEmMayhem
comments.body:
The most impressive thing today probably isn’t a full AI-made game, it’s a game where AI expands the strategy space in a way a handcrafted system wouldn’t. Personally I’m more interested in generated units, personalities, and interactions that force players to adapt than in “AI made all the art/code.” 

I made a game with my game studio and that’s the angle we’re betting on for Make'Em Mayhem: AI as a gameplay system that creates weird, playable combinations instead of just speeding up production. We have a demo out on Steam right now that you can check out:   
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4424310/\_/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4424310/_/)
